'''Vichyssoise''' ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|v|ɪ|ʃ|i|ˈ|s|w|ɑː|z}} {{respell|VISH|ee|SWAHZ}}, {{IPA|fr|viʃiswaz|lang|LL-Q150 (fra)-Ltrlg-vichyssoise.wav}}) is a soup made of cooked and [[purée]]d [[leek (vegetable)|leeks]], [[Potato|potatoes]], [[Onion|onions]] and [[cream]], chilled and garnished with chopped [[chives]]. It was invented in the first quarter of the 20th century by [[Louis Diat]], a French-born cook working as head chef of the [[Ritz-Carlton Hotel (New York City)|Ritz-Carlton Hotel]] in New York.
